title: ALMA-IMF. VII. First release of the full spectral line cubes: Core kinematics traced by DCN J = (3‒2)
question: How to homogeneously calibrate and image the 12m-array spectral line cubes for the 15 ALMA-IMF protoclusters, and what are the global and core-scale kinematics traced by DCN (3-2) across different evolutionary stages?

data.bands: Band 3 (3 mm; ~91-106 GHz) and Band 6 (1.3 mm; ~216-234 GHz)
data.arrays: 12m array released in DR1 (7m and TP arrays also observed, combination ongoing)
data.angular_resolution: ~2000 au physical resolution; 0.3'' to 1.5'' in continuum; ~0.24'' to 2.23'' across line spectral windows
data.sensitivity: 0.88 to 11.18 mJy beam^-1 (dirty beam) in B3; 1.55 to 32.64 mJy beam^-1 (dirty beam) in B6

what.value: Smoothed core catalogues providing positions, major and minor FWHMs, position angles, dust temperatures, masses, and densities for 595 continuum cores

evidence.quote: The core numbering (n), core name, RA, DEC, position angle (PA), core major (F$_{A}$) and core minor (F$_{B}$) FWHM and dust temperatures (T) are taken from the smoothed core catalogues in (cite: louvet22).

evidence.loc: DCN line extraction, background subtraction, and hyperfine fitting
evidence.quote: We used the smoothed core catalogue from (cite: louvet22) to obtain the positions and core sizes for the 595 continuum cores over the 15 ALMA-IMF protoclusters.

what.value: Protocluster central positions, distances, V_LSR, and evolutionary stage classifications (Young, Intermediate, Evolved)

evidence.quote: listing their central positions, $V_{\rm LSR}$ estimates, distances from the Sun, evolutionary nature, and imaged areas of the mosaics in ALMA’s B3 (3 mm) and B6 (1 mm).

what.value: Fraction of bandwidth containing bright line emission (1 - f_BW,cleanest), continuum startmodels (.tt0 and .tt1), and manually defined noise estimation regions

evidence.quote: This is the fraction of the bandwidth found to contain bright line emission, which was excluded to make the `cleanest` continuum cubes, i.e. $1-f_\mathrm{BW,cleanest}$ from Table 3 of (cite: Ginsburg2022).

This model cube is constructed from the .tt0 and .tt1 products of the mostly line-free `cleanest` continuum imaging (see (cite: Ginsburg2022)), `tclean` then stores this as an initial model and subtracts it from the visibilities at the beginning of the deconvolution process.

what.value: Rest frequencies and hyperfine structure frequencies and relative weights for DCN (3-2)

evidence.loc: DCN line extraction, background subtraction, and hyperfine fitting
evidence.quote: The values for the specified hyperfine model were taken from the CDMS catalogue to define the frequencies and relative weights of the hyperfine lines (cite: Endres2016; muller2001; muller2005).

what.value: Upper level energies and critical densities for OCS, OC33S, C18O, 13CS, DCN, N2D+, and DCO+

evidence.loc: Protocluster $V_{\rm LSR}$ estimates from the DCN (3-2) fits
evidence.quote: The temperatures and critical densities for OCS, OC$^{33}$S, C$^{18}$O and $^{13}$CS are taken from (cite: molet19).

evidence.loc: Protocluster $V_{\rm LSR}$ estimates from the DCN (3-2) fits
evidence.quote: For DCN (3-2), we take the values from (cite: Bocso2019) and for N$_2$D$^+$, DCO$^+$ we follow (cite: Bocso2019) and approximate the critical density assuming $n_{crit}\approx$A/$\Gamma$ (cite: Shirley2015), for collisional rates at T=100 K where the Einstein A and $\Gamma$ coefficients are taken from the Leiden Atomic Molecular Database (LAMBDA) (cite: Schoier2005).

recipe.goal: Calibrate, image, and post-process the 12m spectral line cubes
recipe.method: Restore QA3-reprocessed measurement sets with scriptForPI.py, split spectral windows and combine 12m configurations, build continuum startmodel from cleanest continuum (.tt0 and .tt1), deconvolve line cubes with multi-scale tclean using a 10% pbmask, convolve models to a common beam with radio-beam, apply JvM correction to residuals, and subtract continuum in the image plane with STATCONT
key_parameters: Cleaning threshold = 5 sigma (10 sigma for G351.77)
Multi-scale scales = geometric series from 0 increasing by ~x2 minor beam/cell size up to ~5.5''
assumptions: Dirty beam volume is integrated up to its first null to compute JvM epsilon factor

recipe.goal: Estimate cube noise levels homogeneously across all fields and spectral windows
recipe.method: Calculate MAD (scaled by 1.4826) on the 25% of channels with the lowest intensity within manually defined continuum noise regions on JvM-corrected, non-continuum-subtracted, non-primary-beam-corrected cubes, then scale by 1/epsilon to convert to mJy per dirty beam
key_parameters: 25% lowest intensity channels; MAD scale factor = 1.4826
assumptions: Noise estimated from a smaller clean beam should be scaled up by the dirty-to-clean beam volume ratio (1/epsilon)

recipe.method: Shift B6 spw1 STATCONT continuum-subtracted, non-primary-beam-corrected cubes to DCN (3-2) rest frame, extract a 50 km s^-1 subcube around protocluster V_LSR, and compute moment 0, 1, and 2 maps over manually determined velocity ranges using a 4 sigma threshold
key_parameters: Subcube width = 50 km s^-1; pixel and channel threshold = 4 sigma (dirty beam noise); rest frequency = 217.23854 GHz

recipe.goal: Extract core-averaged background-subtracted DCN (3-2) spectra and fit hyperfine structure
recipe.method: Extract average DCN (3-2) spectrum for each of the 595 continuum cores from an elliptical aperture of 2x the continuum FWHM, subtract background spectrum from an elliptical annulus (2x to 3x continuum FWHM, excluding overlapping neighbour cores), fit single-component DCN hyperfine structure model in PySpecKit, and classify detections into Single- or Complex-type
key_parameters: Core aperture = 2x continuum FWHM; background annulus = 2x to 3x continuum FWHM; detection criteria: S/N > 4 sigma (from MAD in 30 line-free channels) and velocity dispersion > 0.2 km s^-1; 7 hyperfine components from CDMS
assumptions: DCN (3-2) is an optically thin dense gas tracer with critical density ~10^7 cm^-3; FWHM linewidth = sigma_obs * sqrt(8 ln 2)

recipe.goal: Analyze core-to-core velocity dispersion, spatial spread, and non-thermal velocity dispersion across evolutionary stages
recipe.method: Compute core velocity offsets, core-to-core velocity dispersions, radial spatial offsets, and non-thermal velocity dispersions for the 266 Single-type cores; apply Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) tests between evolutionary stages and compute Pearson's correlation coefficient between non-thermal velocity dispersion and deconvolved core size
key_parameters: T_k = 18 K to 300 K (from continuum dust temperature); smoothed continuum beam = 2700 au
assumptions: Gas kinetic temperature T_k for DCN (3-2) equals the core dust temperature from Louvet et al.; core size is the geometric mean of major and minor continuum FWHMs deconvolved by the smoothed beam (unless deconvolved size < 0.5x non-deconvolved size)

answer_key.quantity: Average ratio of line beam to continuum beam (excluding B3 spw0)

evidence.quote: The average ratio of the line beams and continuum beam is $\sim$1.2, except for B3, spectral window 0 (which includes the N$_2$H$^+$ transition), where the ratio is on average $\sim$1.4.

answer_key.quantity: Total continuum cores with DCN (3-2) detection (Single + Complex)

evidence.quote: Of the 595 continuum cores, 357 (60%) have a DCN (3-2) detection.

answer_key.quantity: Total continuum cores with Single-type DCN (3-2) detection

evidence.quote: After filtering out the cores with a Complex DCN (3-2) spectrum, the sample is reduced to 266 continuum cores, that is, $\sim$45% of the continuum cores have a single component HFS fit.

Average Single-type DCN (3-2) core detection rate in Intermediate protoclusters
Average Single-type DCN (3-2) core detection rate in Evolved protoclusters
Core-to-core velocity dispersion for Young protoclusters

evidence.quote: We find core-to-core velocity dispersions of 1.8$\pm$0.2 km s$^{-1}$, 2.6$\pm$0.4km s$^{-1}$, and 2.2$\pm$0.2km s$^{-1}$ for the young, intermediate, and evolved protoclusters, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Core-to-core velocity dispersion for Intermediate protoclusters

evidence.quote: We find core-to-core velocity dispersions of 1.8$\pm$0.2 km s$^{-1}$, 2.6$\pm$0.4km s$^{-1}$, and 2.2$\pm$0.2km s$^{-1}$ for the young, intermediate, and evolved protoclusters, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Core-to-core velocity dispersion for Evolved protoclusters

evidence.quote: We find core-to-core velocity dispersions of 1.8$\pm$0.2 km s$^{-1}$, 2.6$\pm$0.4km s$^{-1}$, and 2.2$\pm$0.2km s$^{-1}$ for the young, intermediate, and evolved protoclusters, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Standard deviation of core spatial spread (Young, Intermediate, Evolved)

evidence.quote: The standard deviation of the spatial spread for the young, intermediate, and evolved regions are 0.33 pc, 0.39 pc, and 0.60 pc, respectively, with standard errors $<$0.06 pc.

answer_key.quantity: Average DCN (3-2) core linewidth in Young and Intermediate protoclusters

evidence.quote: Considering the DCN (3-2) linewidths grouped by evolutionary classification, we find slightly smaller average linewidths in the evolved regions of $\sim$1.2 km s$^{-1}$ compared to the young and intermediate protoclusters of $\sim$1.5 km s$^{-1}$, and standard deviations of $\sim$0.5, and $\sim$0.7 km s$^{-1}$ respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Average DCN (3-2) core linewidth in Evolved protoclusters

evidence.quote: Considering the DCN (3-2) linewidths grouped by evolutionary classification, we find slightly smaller average linewidths in the evolved regions of $\sim$1.2 km s$^{-1}$ compared to the young and intermediate protoclusters of $\sim$1.5 km s$^{-1}$, and standard deviations of $\sim$0.5, and $\sim$0.7 km s$^{-1}$ respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Pearson correlation coefficient between non-thermal velocity dispersion and core size

evidence.quote: We fit Pearson’s correlation coefficient ($\rho$), which measures the linear correlation between two variables, and find a value of 0.18, indicating no correlation exists between the dispersion and core sizes in these data.

answer_key.quantity: Average core mass and density for Complex-type, Single-type, and non-detected DCN cores

evidence.loc: Nature of the core population traced by DCN (3-2)
evidence.quote: We find that the Complex-type spectra are typically extracted in cores with higher masses and densities ($\sim$17 M$_{\odot}$, and $\sim$2.5$\times$10$^7$cm$^{-3}$, respectively) than those with Single-type DCN (3-2) spectra ($\sim$5 M$_{\odot}$, and $\sim$1$\times$10$^7$cm$^{-3}$, respectively).

evidence.loc: Nature of the core population traced by DCN (3-2)
evidence.quote: If we consider the non-detected cores, the average masses and densities are slightly lower, $\sim$3 M$_{\odot}$, and $\sim$0.8$\times$10$^7$cm$^{-3}$, respectively.
